Decoding the PROCTITLE hex yields "cat /media/share/healthcheck_cron.sh". The log shows root executing `cat` on a script located in a shared media mount (/media/share), with no interactive user session (auid=unset, ses=unset). Reading a cron health-check script via cat is a benign-looking administrative action, but it is performed as root from a non-login context on a writable share, which can precede script tampering or credential harvesting (e.g., T1552.001 Credentials in Files, T1059.004 Unix Shell, T1037.004 RC Scripts/cron abuse). The evidence is a single, low-complexity read operation with no follow-on activity, so it leans toward normal administrative behavior.
